audit_target: The two committed MRR archive dumps — the only versioned, byte-stable form the authoritative archive of the two real runs exists in.
provenance: Written 2026-07-25 at the N2-T02 derivation. Each sha256 below was computed at derivation from the committed file's real bytes and is pinned as a fail-closed integrity anchor: if a dump is regenerated (make archive-dump) or edited, the anchor stops matching and the audit refuses rather than reporting over changed data. Git is authoritative for these committed bytes. Extended 2026-08-01 (N1-T02 side finding): run 3 was produced after this batch was frozen on 2026-07-25 and had been sitting outside the nightly integrity check ever since — the check reported green over two thirds of the archive. Its anchor was computed the same way, from the committed file's real bytes.
note_on_the_input_choice: The audit reads these committed dumps and NOT the local PostgreSQL instance, although that instance was reachable at derivation (127.0.0.1:54329 accepted connections). That instance is explicitly a throwaway (docs/design/2026-07-22-nutzungsentscheidung-e9-vertagt.md, Befund 1 — artefact durability is still an open owner decision): auditing it would audit an ephemeral artefact nobody else can reproduce. The dumps are committed, hash-anchorable, and re-checkable by anyone holding the repository, and reading them requires no database connection at all.
